text: Someone is hunting the Operator, but he has rent to pay. Monday, he's underground again, with Nib out front playing husk.
Nib's bare foot sinks a loose brick, exactly as a husk's would.
Darts fly from the wall. Nib dodges without breaking stride. Not very husk-like.
Worse, he corrects the client's grip. A Ninth Wall soldier can't watch a sword held like that.
The clients gape, Bomi's drone swings round in delight, and Jaeha's excuse is worse than last time.
Picture it: Jaeha the ventriloquist, and a dummy that looks ready to kill.
Nib freezes back into a doll, but two thousand viewers saw it, and the chat isn't buying it.
Why is the Operator testing traps again? Rent. Fifty thousand won to walk in, ten thousand a trap.
Bomi has tagged along for the content. Her headline writes itself.
Yerin, holding her bag out of the splashes, regrets everything. Jaeha reminds her they're both broke.
His notebook now has rules for living with a goblin, and both are about not getting caught.
Jaeha hisses through his smile that the first one didn't last long. Nib is not sorry.
Nib's eye slides toward a dark side tunnel. His ear twitches. Something's down there.
Behind him, the clients have found a new nickname for him. It's the old one.
He isn't sitting. He's marking a hair-thin wire at ankle height. Each one is worth money.
Nib walks into it like a good husk, and a net crashes down just behind his heels.
Jaeha, flat-faced, adds another ten thousand won to the count and puts it down to luck.
At a junction where five tunnels meet, violet eyes glint from every dark mouth.
Then the ash rats pour out, dozens of them: hairless, grey, knee-high, all yellow teeth.
The client leader swings wild and misses. The spearman falls on his backside.
Bomi fires with her eyes shut. The arrow hits the ceiling, and a brick flattens a rat.
Technically, the ceiling scored. Bomi is claiming it anyway.
And that gives Jaeha an idea. He sends her camera chasing a monster that isn't there.
The drone zooms off down a tunnel with nothing in it.
With the camera gone, Nib can stop pretending: five minutes of field form.
Nib tears through the swarm like a blade, and the rats burst into violet ash.
From above, it's a spiral of ash, the swarm thinning ring by ring.
One rat slips past and clamps onto the spearman's calf.
Yerin drops into the water beside him, hands glowing, her voice steadier than his.
But Bomi's feed shows an empty tunnel, and she wants her drone back.
Jaeha, sweating, keeps the lie going with total confidence.
All the while he reads the swarm like a timetable, silently sending Nib to meet the next rush.
Nib lands right there, slashes both ways, and the rats pile up. Nobody sees the drone's red light come back.
Yerin watches with her hands over her mouth. The clients have their eyes squeezed shut.
Then it's over. Not one rat left, and Nib used barely a minute of his five.
The drone comes back to drifting ash, two clients uncurling, and one very still husk.
Then the swarm mother squeezes out: twice their size, with bony spurs down its back.
With Nib on cooldown, Jaeha points the client at the dart trap from earlier and calls the timing.
The darts slam home, and the leader drives his sword into its neck. With the right grip.
The leader stares at his sword: he killed a boss. A kind Jaeha hasn't met before, so Route Alignment doubles to sixty percent.
They splash for the exit as the tunnel flakes into light, Jaeha towing the limping spearman.
The client sheepishly admits the doll was right. Jaeha bows on its behalf.
Outside at dusk, soaked to the shins, he's paid by the trap: a hundred and twenty thousand won.
The bandaged spearman thanks Yerin for not flinching. He has no idea about her first raid.
Jaeha looks down at the thin fold of notes and does the subtraction. It isn't close.
Bomi's stream peaked near five thousand, and the chat has named the crew: the trap rats.
Bomi loves it and declares them a team. Jaeha has been called trap rat by people who meant it.
Bomi winks. To a streamer, an insult that trends is a gift.
Yerin closes his fingers back over her share. She has no job either, and still won't take it.
Then Bomi tries to interview the husk. Jaeha slides in, palms up, before Nib gives her a quote.
That night the landlady waits at the top of the stairs. Jaeha offers her today's pay, plus a promise.
She snatches the cash, then squints past him at the small masked figure on the stairs.
A veteran of the Ninth Wall has just been called a pet.
Nearby, a family restaurant sits dark with a for-sale sort of notice on its door. A light is on upstairs.
It's Bomi's room, and all that clout-chasing has a target. It was never about fame.
On her desk, a photo of a little girl and her parents on opening day.
She stops the sewer footage on one blurred frame. Her drone came back sooner than Jaeha knew.
She zooms in. A cracked white mask, and beside it, one glowing amber eye.
Bomi's eyes narrow. She can't hit a rat with an arrow, but she just hit something bigger.
